opportunities.title: Understanding and avoiding maladaptation to climate change - HORIZON-CL5-2027-01-D1-10
opportunities.program: Horizon Europe Cluster 5 - Destination 1 'Climate sciences and responses', call HORIZON-CL5-2027-01
opportunities.funding_text: RIA; topic budget EUR 18,000,000 (2027); expected 3 grants; EU contribution per project EUR 5,000,000 - 6,000,000
opportunities.eligible_applicants: Legal entities in consortia per Horizon Europe General Annexes (standard RIA: at least 3 independent entities from 3 different EU Member States/Associated Countries, at least one from a Member State)
opportunities.eligible_countries: EU Member States and Associated Countries automatically eligible for funding; LMICs listed in General Annexes eligible; other third countries per Programme Guide
opportunities.cgiar_eligibility_notes: Bioversity International (registered in Italy) can join as a funded beneficiary; Horizon Europe personnel costs are eligible actual costs. CIAT (Colombia) is not automatically eligible for funding (Colombia not on LMIC list), so run any Colombian/LAC case-study work through Bioversity or as associated partner.
opportunities.lead_applicant_requirements: Not specified beyond Horizon Europe standard rules
opportunities.geographic_restrictions: Topic is EU-policy oriented (EU Adaptation Strategy, Climate-ADAPT), but scope explicitly covers evidence 'across sectors and regions, both in Europe and globally'
opportunities.consortium_details: Standard Horizon Europe RIA consortium; coordination with Mission Adaptation and Cluster 5 Destination 1 projects encouraged
opportunities.cofunding_details: RIA funded at 100% of eligible costs (Horizon Europe standard)
opportunities.eligible_activities: Identify drivers of maladaptation across systems; map/validate evidence via case studies (local/regional/national); strengthen methodological toolbox for complex climate risk and adaptation assessment; propose corrective responses and prevention guidelines; feed EU repositories (Climate-ADAPT) and European Climate Risk Assessments. If satellite EO is used, Copernicus and/or Galileo/EGNOS must be used.
opportunities.required_documents: Horizon Europe Part A (online forms) and Part B (technical description) via F&T Submission System
opportunities.application_procedure: Single-stage submission through the EU Funding & Tenders Portal
opportunities.scientific_alignment_rationale: Adaptation evidence and risk-assessment methods are core; Alliance crop-model/EO evidence on maladaptation in agriculture (e.g., irrigation, land-use shifts, crop switching) fits a case-study work package, but topic is SSH/policy heavy rather than RS/AI-centric.
opportunities.strategic_relevance_rationale: Global evidence on agricultural maladaptation from LAC/Africa/Asia is a distinctive CGIAR contribution; IPCC-relevant.
opportunities.technical_feasibility_rationale: Team can deliver crop-modelling and remote-sensing based adaptation outcome assessments as case studies.
opportunities.recommendation: Pursue as partner (Bioversity Italy as beneficiary) in a European consortium; offer global agri-food case studies on maladaptation detected via EO + crop modelling. Opens 17 Nov 2026, deadline 4 Mar 2027 - start partner search now.
opportunities.potential_partners: Climate-ADAPT/EEA-linked institutes, PIK, CMCC (Italy), IIASA, Wageningen UR, BC3, SEI
opportunities.next_action: Register topic in F&T partner search after 17 Nov 2026 opening; contact CMCC/PIK/WUR adaptation groups proposing a global agriculture maladaptation case-study WP.

opportunities.title: Cost-effective biodiversity monitoring for EU policies - HORIZON-NATURE-2027-02-05
opportunities.program: Horizon Europe - 'Transformative change towards a nature-positive economy and society' call HORIZON-NATURE-2027-02
opportunities.funding_text: RIA; topic budget EUR 16,000,000 (2027); expected 3 grants; EU contribution per project EUR 5,000,000 - 6,000,000
opportunities.eligible_applicants: Consortia of legal entities per Horizon Europe General Annexes
opportunities.eligible_countries: EU Member States and Associated Countries; LMICs per General Annexes
opportunities.cgiar_eligibility_notes: Bioversity International (Italy) eligible as beneficiary; however demonstration cases must serve EU legislation (Nature Restoration Regulation pollinator monitoring, Soil Monitoring Law soil biodiversity, Water Framework Directive), so Alliance role is methods/AI partner rather than lead.
opportunities.lead_applicant_requirements: Not specified beyond Horizon Europe standard rules
opportunities.geographic_restrictions: EU monitoring schemes (NRR, SML, WFD) - European demonstration sites
opportunities.consortium_details: Proposals must indicate Area A (NRR/EU Pollinators Monitoring Scheme), B (soil biodiversity for SML) or C (WFD); awards balanced across areas
opportunities.eligible_activities: Develop scalable cost-effective biodiversity monitoring integrating technologies; demonstration cases; automated and real-time monitoring frameworks supported by AI; compare approaches; DNA-based species identification; Copernicus use mandatory if satellite EO used
opportunities.required_documents: Horizon Europe Part A and Part B via F&T Submission System
opportunities.application_procedure: Single-stage submission via EU Funding & Tenders Portal (submission session open since 13 Oct 2026)
opportunities.scientific_alignment_rationale: AI/automated and remote-sensing-supported monitoring matches skills; but focus is in-situ, DNA and pollinator/soil/freshwater biodiversity in EU legal schemes.
opportunities.strategic_relevance_rationale: EU-internal policy focus; limited LAC/Africa/Asia relevance; useful for Bioversity's agrobiodiversity monitoring portfolio.
opportunities.technical_feasibility_rationale: Alliance could contribute AI/EO data fusion; would rely on European partners for field schemes.
opportunities.recommendation: Low-medium priority; join only if an EU consortium needs an AI/EO data-integration partner (e.g., Area A pollinator habitat mapping). Deadline is close (14 Jan 2027).
opportunities.potential_partners: Biodiversa+ members, JRC-linked institutes, UFZ, CREA (Italy), Naturalis
opportunities.next_action: Check F&T partner search for HORIZON-NATURE-2027-02-05 consortia seeking AI/EO partners before mid-December 2026.

opportunities.title: Strengthening rural communities' resilience to shocks - HORIZON-CL6-2027-02-COMMUNITIES-01
opportunities.program: Horizon Europe Cluster 6 - Call HORIZON-CL6-2027-02 (single stage)
opportunities.funding_text: RIA; topic budget EUR 15,000,000 (2027); expected 3 grants of about EUR 5,000,000
opportunities.eligible_applicants: Consortia per Horizon Europe General Annexes; multi-actor approach mandatory
opportunities.eligible_countries: EU Member States and Associated Countries; LMICs per General Annexes
opportunities.cgiar_eligibility_notes: Bioversity International (Italy) eligible as beneficiary. Topic is EU rural-areas oriented, but 'International cooperation is encouraged to foster knowledge exchange and peer-to-peer learning across countries' - Alliance could bring LAC/Africa comparative cases.
opportunities.lead_applicant_requirements: Not specified beyond Horizon Europe standard rules
opportunities.geographic_restrictions: Primarily EU rural areas (long-term vision for EU rural areas 2040)
opportunities.consortium_details: Multi-actor approach required: researchers, local authorities, rural communities, civil protection; SSH expertise required
opportunities.eligible_activities: Assess shocks (climate, environmental, socio-economic) on rural communities; resilience indicators; inclusive anticipatory governance and DRR plans; community-based adaptation; contribute to JRC Resilience Dashboards
opportunities.required_documents: Horizon Europe Part A and Part B
opportunities.application_procedure: Single-stage submission via F&T Portal after opening on 20 April 2027
opportunities.scientific_alignment_rationale: Community resilience/SSH focus; EO-based shock detection and resilience indicators are a possible but secondary contribution.
opportunities.strategic_relevance_rationale: EU rural focus; international cooperation only encouraged.
opportunities.technical_feasibility_rationale: Could provide climate-shock indicators and anticipatory analytics; SSH/multi-actor lead needed from EU partners.
opportunities.recommendation: Monitor; low priority unless an EU consortium seeks a Global South comparative/anticipatory-analytics partner.
opportunities.potential_partners: JRC Resilience Dashboard teams, Wageningen UR, CREA, rural development networks
opportunities.next_action: Re-check when the call opens (20 Apr 2027) and scan partner search.

opportunities.title: Sustainability and resilience of climate projections and related data records for European and global science and policy - HORIZON-BRIDGING-2027-04-08
opportunities.funding_text: CSA; topic budget EUR 5,000,000; expected 1 grant
opportunities.eligible_applicants: Consortia per Horizon Europe General Annexes; LMIC entities 'may exceptionally participate in this Coordination and Support Action as beneficiary or affiliated entity'
opportunities.eligible_countries: EU Member States and Associated Countries; LMICs automatically eligible may exceptionally participate
opportunities.cgiar_eligibility_notes: Bioversity International (Italy) could be a beneficiary; realistically a minor partner/user-community role (climate projection data for agricultural impact modelling in vulnerable countries).
opportunities.geographic_restrictions: European + global coordination of ESGF; 'strong focus on inclusiveness, equity, and the needs of the most vulnerable countries'
opportunities.consortium_details: Single CSA expected to be led by European climate modelling/data community (e.g., ENES/ESGF nodes)
opportunities.eligible_activities: Track availability of CMIP/CORDEX projections and risks; coordinate Europe-wide mitigation of data-access risks; strengthen Earth System Grid Federation (ESGF) resilience in Europe and globally; links to ESFRI and EOSC
opportunities.required_documents: Horizon Europe Part A and Part B
opportunities.application_procedure: Single-stage submission via F&T Portal (submission session open since 6 Oct 2026)
opportunities.scientific_alignment_rationale: Climate data infrastructure is an interest area, but this is an ESGF governance/infrastructure CSA, not crop/EO research.
opportunities.strategic_relevance_rationale: Single grant almost certainly led by ENES/ESGF; Alliance role limited to user-needs input for Global South agriculture.
opportunities.technical_feasibility_rationale: Alliance does not operate ESGF nodes.
opportunities.recommendation: Do not lead; only offer a small user-community/LMIC-needs task if approached by the ESGF consortium.
opportunities.next_action: Optional: contact CMCC (Italy) to offer a Global South agricultural-user task before January 2027.

opportunities.title: IKI Medium Grants 2026 (7th ideas competition) - Green skills for local climate action incl. sustainable agriculture
opportunities.funder: German Federal Ministry for the Environment (BMUKN) - International Climate Initiative (IKI)
opportunities.deadline_text: The ideas competition (call) opens on 13 October 2026 and closes on 12 January 2027 at 11.59 am (CET).
opportunities.funding_text: Total budget of up to EUR 8 million; individual projects EUR 300,000 - 800,000
opportunities.eligible_applicants: civil society organisations, academic institutions and not-for-profit organisations based in Germany
opportunities.eligible_countries: Developing and emerging economies in the Global South; 1-2 implementing countries
opportunities.cgiar_eligibility_notes: Lead must be based in Germany (permanent establishment by first disbursement). Alliance cannot lead unless it has a German establishment; possible role as local partner organisation in Colombia/implementing country, but partner rules not stated on page.
opportunities.lead_applicant_requirements: Applicant must have a permanent business establishment, branch or other facility in Germany by the time of first disbursement; must partner with 1-2 local implementing organisations
opportunities.geographic_restrictions: Global South, bilateral or regional (1-2 countries)
opportunities.consortium_details: German applicant plus one or two local partner organisations in implementing country/countries
opportunities.eligible_activities: Priority I 'Green skills for local climate action': practical approaches such as community-based renewable energy, sustainable agriculture; Priority II 'Future-proof coasts': marine/coastal ecosystem protection with digital biodiversity monitoring
opportunities.required_documents: Project outline via online portal; concept note and sample outline form templates
opportunities.application_procedure: Two-phase: outline via IKI ideas platform by 12 Jan 2027; selected outlines invited to full proposal. Online info seminar 19 November, 10:00-11:30 CET.
opportunities.scientific_alignment_rationale: Climate-smart/sustainable agriculture skills fits thematically; research methods (RS/AI/crop modelling) are secondary in a skills-focused implementation grant.
opportunities.strategic_relevance_rationale: Useful partner route with German universities/NGOs for Colombia/Central America climate-smart agriculture skills; small multi-year budget.
opportunities.technical_feasibility_rationale: Alliance can supply training content on digital advisory/CSA as local partner.
opportunities.recommendation: Partner opportunity only: approach German university or NGO partners (e.g., GIZ-linked NGOs, Univ. Hohenheim, Univ. Bonn ZEF) to lead with Alliance/CIAT as local implementing partner in Colombia. Confirm partner eligibility in the IMG Administrative Guidelines.
opportunities.potential_partners: ZEF Univ. Bonn, Univ. Hohenheim, Welthungerhilfe, Leibniz ZALF
opportunities.next_action: Register for 19 Nov 2026 IKI seminar; read IMG Administrative Guidelines (05/2026) on partner eligibility and personnel costs; contact a German lead by early December.
